text:
Maya: Pushed a draft GH Action for nightly CI traces: nsys timelines, nvprof kernel stats, and a compact perfetto CPU trace. Want quick eyes on warmup/noise, kv cache modes, and artifact retention.

Sam: can you paste the workflow + runner script? also how do you make request ordering deterministic for steady-state runs?

Maya: workflow snippet below. key points: run per-model variants, do deterministic tokenization with fixed seed, capture 3 warmup + 6 measured iters, tag artifacts with metadata (quant/profile/kv_mode). upload raw traces then generate CSV summaries.

Maya: ```yaml
name: nightly-trace-capture
on: ubuntu-22.04
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v3
  - run: ./ci/run_traces.sh --model ${MODEL} --warmup 3 --measured 6 --seed 42 --nsys --nvprof --perfetto --kv-mode ${KV_MODE} --prompt-corpus ${CORPUS_ID}
  - run: ./ci/postproc_traces.py --in artifacts/${BUILD_ID} --out artifacts/${BUILD_ID}/summary/
  - run: aws s3 sync artifacts/${BUILD_ID}/ s3://redwood-perf-traces/${MODEL}/${BUILD_ID}/ --acl private
```

Liam: 3+6 is better than tiny runs, but noisy GPUs still need more samples for p99 stability. consider doubling measured iters for larger models and adding a variance check that triggers a rerun if p50 stddev > 8%.

Maya: good idea. will add an adaptive re-run: if measured p50 variability > 8% across measured iters, automatically schedule an extended run (measured=12).

Ana: KV cache affects kernel selection drastically. We should run two modes: cold (no KV priming) and steady (simulate long session with session_length > 128 requests). Also run a "rolling" ordering where requests mimic a real distribution rather than fixed corpus ordering.

Maya: added flags: --kv-mode {cold,steady,rolling} and --session-length. artifacts include kv_mode tag.

perfbot: perfbot: trace artifacts uploaded for build 1794567890. s3://redwood-perf-traces/gptx/1794567890/ (raw traces + summary CSVs)

Sam: are we collecting CUPTI kernel timestamps + NVTX ranges so we can correlate host-side events with kernel launches? nvprof summaries are useful but we need timeline alignment for flamegraphs.

Maya: yes: nsys capture includes NVTX markers from the runtime and CUPTI counts enabled for top kernels. postproc merges nsys perfetto JSON + nvprof kernel table into a unified timeline and produces metrics.csv.

Liam: metrics.csv should be canonical for the diff dashboard. suggest columns: build_id, model, quant_profile, kv_mode, batch_size, seq_len, kernel_name, run_count, avg_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, sm_eff, occupancy, bytes_transferred. Keep kernel names normalized (strip version suffixes).

Maya: will normalize kernel names and emit metrics.csv and a trimmed timeline.json (only top kernels). Dashboard will diff metrics.csv between builds and highlight top-3 kernel regressions and any kernel selection changes.

Ana: be careful with quantization: int8 vs fp16 picks different kernels. Dashboard should group comparables only. Add metadata tags for quant_profile and quant_backend.

Maya: yep noted. we tag runs with quant_profile, kernel_hint, and runtime-kernel-selection. diffs will only compare runs with matching quant_profile unless user explicitly requests cross-profile diffs.

DevOps: storage note: full nsys captures are large. proposed retention: keep raw captures 60d, compressed trimmed traces 1y, CSV summaries 2y. apply s3 lifecycle to move raw->glacier after 60d. ok?

Maya: approved. Also compress perfetto JSONs with gzip before upload to save space. Postproc will operate on local uncompressed copies on the runner then push compressed outputs.

Liam: alerting rules: create warning if p99 for a kernel increases > 15% vs baseline and severity if > 35%. Also create an anomaly if kernel selection for a hot op changes (e.g., fast_gemm_v3 -> generic_gemm). For selection changes, include a short repro command in the alert body.

Maya: will implement alert logic in the differ service. default action: create a ticket + post summary to #eng-runtime. Fail-the-build only for severe infra regressions (>=35% p99 or sudden drop in throughput > 25%).

Sam: for triage make it easy to repro locally: add `./ci/run_traces.sh --model gptx --kv-mode steady --measured 12 --seed 42 --build-tag local-test` to the README. Also include a helper `./ci/compare_csvs.py baseline.csv new.csv` that emits a compact diff and top kernel deltas.

Maya: added `compare_csvs.py` and a local repro section in docs.

perfbot: perfbot: nightly summary: 5 models run, kv_modes: 3 steady, 2 cold, 1 run triggered extended sampling due to high variance. Diffs queued for the dashboard.

Ana: i'll watch the dashboard first pass — if you see kernel migration noise >10% across many runs, we'll need to increase measured samples or refine ordering.

Maya: thanks all. I'll land the GH Action and post the follow-up PR with dashboard wiring and alert rules. :rocket:
